subject: How to add occurance data of two species in Wallace

messages.author: ef79cd1b98b42ff7
messages.subject: How to add occurance data of two species in Wallace
parts:
Dear Wallace Team,

I have done SDM for snow leopard data in Wallace. Now I want to try Himalayan Ibex and Snow Leopard data at the same time. Can anyone help me figure out how to upload the target species' occurrence data at the same time? 

Thanks

Tauheed

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: How to add occurance data of two species in Wallace
parts:
Hi Tauheed,

First, make sure you are running version 2.0.4 (v1.1.3 cannot support running multiple species).
Occurrence data are uploaded in the Obtain Occurrence Data component. 
If you are using the first module, Query Database (Present), select which database to query, type in the species names.  You can do multiple species individually and specify the maximum number of species separately, or you can type several species, separated by a comma, and set the maximum number of occurrences for all.
The same goes for the second module, Query Database (Paleo).
If you are using the third module, you can upload several csv files or one file with multiple species included. Just remember the first three field names need to be scientific_name, longitude, and latitude.
You can also use a combination of the modules (e.g., query GBIF and then upload a user csv)

Once the species are uploaded, you should see a message in the log window. The map will not change unless you change it, which can be done using the species drop-down menu. This menu changes which species are shown on the map and specifies which species to run the analyses on.

For a more detailed description, see the Obtain Occurrence Data section of the user vignette: https://wallaceecomod.github.io/wallace/articles/tutorial-v2.html#obtain-occurrence-data

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: How to add occurance data of two species in Wallace
parts:
v2.0.4 allows users to model several species simultaneously, but yes they are separate models for each species. You can replicate the steps of analysis for each species- this is easily done by checking the "Batch" box at the bottom of the modules. This "Batch" button will run the selections you have made for ALL the species you have uploaded. 
The Environmental Space component allows you to characterize the environmental space and you can calculate environmental ordination or niche overlap between species. This component can only be used if you have uploaded more than one species.
